String.en: Not loaded: the ~r~Plugins/LSFD~s~ folder is missing or incomplete. Reinstall LSFD from the download.
Loaded. Visit a ~r~fire station~s~ to go on duty. Tablet: ~b~{0}
Bug report saved to ~y~Plugins/LSFD/BugReport.txt~s~. Attach it to your report.
Response: {0}~n~Water: ~b~{1:N0} L~s~ · On the call {2} min~n~Rescued ~g~{3}~s~ · Treated {4}
Clock out and change back into your own clothes.
Suit up in the locker room and clock in at this station.
Have a vehicle and its crew brought out in front of the station.
Choose the outfit you wear on duty (EUP outfits too).
A full SCBA cylinder, your health and a flashlight.
Connect a supply line to a hydrant to refill the tank.
Switch the nozzle to foam with {0} for fuel and vehicle fires.
{0:0} m line with an adjustable straight/fog nozzle.
{0:0} m line to connect this apparatus to a fire hydrant.
Replace the cylinder on your back with a full one.
Blows the smoke out of a building: set it up in the doorway, facing in. The fresh air also feeds the fire.
Shows victims, flames and hotspots through the smoke. Turn it on with {0}.
Put it back in the compartment.
Take it from or put it back in the compartment.
Model {0}. Rename or edit it in Plugins/LSFD/Profiles/Outfits.xml.
Dress up with the EUP menu (or any outfit tool) first, then save it here as your duty outfit.
Saved as ~y~{0}~s~ and selected. Rename it in Profiles/Outfits.xml.
Go on duty at a fire station to receive calls.
Report the call as handled or cancelled.
An AI engine with crew responds and works the scene.
An AI ambulance crew responds and takes care of patients.
You are available. Dispatch will send you the next call.
Ask dispatch for a call right away.
There are no calls waiting right now.
From accepting the call to arriving on scene, against a target for the distance.
Pumped by every apparatus on the call, from the tank or a hydrant.
The fire grew to a bigger alarm.
Response time, lives lost, fire escalation and whether the call was completed; rescues earn extra. Completed calls add a tenth of the score to your career points.
Request an apparatus at a fire station, or walk up to a fire truck.
Connect a supply line to a hydrant to refill.
Feeds water to the attack hose.
Discharge pressure to the attack hose.
Sends this apparatus and its crew back to quarters.
Growing → burning → under control → knockdown → out.
Goes up when the fire grows too big; every alarm brings another engine.
Knocked down, but they rekindle unless you overhaul them with water. The thermal camera shows them.
Flammable: use foam. Electrical: isolate the power first. Battery: lots of water, keeps rekindling.
Isolate it at the panel (yellow arrow) before using water.
A PPV fan in the doorway pushes the smoke out, but feeds the fire.
Carry them out to the staging area.
Waiting for an ambulance to take them to hospital.
Being loaded or in the ambulance.
Hold E at a patient, or order the crew to patient care.
Apparatus come with AI firefighters when requested at a station.
Do what is most urgent: CPR, rescues, extrication, treatment, then the fire.
Carry victims out of buildings and extricate trapped occupants.
CPR and first aid for every patient on scene.
Stretch hose lines from the engines (extinguishers when none are left) and attack the closest fires.
One firefighter per engine works the roof-mounted water cannon.
Calls, fires, rescues and patients all count.
{0} ({1}). Select to set a GPS waypoint.
The call was given to another unit.
All {0} ~y~traffic cones~s~ are out. Pick one up to place it elsewhere.
Call cancelled, you went off duty.
Press ~b~{0}~s~ or use the tablet to respond.
Press ~b~{0}~s~ to stop and handle it yourself.
You were incapacitated, another unit is taking over.
Could not read the callouts in ~y~{0}~s~, see RagePluginHook.log.
Callout pack ~y~{0}~s~ was not loaded: it {1}
~g~On duty~s~ at ~y~{0}~s~. Open the tablet with ~b~{1}~s~.
There is no {0} available in Apparatus.xml.
The fire at ~y~{0}~s~ is spreading. Another engine company is responding.
Command reports the fire is ~y~under control~s~. Keep working it.
No open flames left. ~o~Overhaul~s~: soak every hotspot, the thermal camera shows them.
All hotspots are overhauled, the fire is out.
~r~Rekindle!~s~ A hotspot burst into flames again.
You need the ~y~{0}~s~ from an engine for this.
The hose was pulled out of your hands, it doesn't reach any further.
~o~The hose is almost fully stretched out.
~o~The pump of the {0} is disengaged.~s~ Engage it on the tablet.
The {0} is ~o~out of foam~s~, back to water.
~r~The {0} is out of water.~s~ Connect it to a hydrant.
Bring the supply line of the ~y~{0}~s~ to a ~b~fire hydrant~s~ (max {1:0} m).
Supply line of the ~y~{0}~s~ disconnected and stowed.
connect the supply line to the ~b~hydrant
The supply line doesn't reach that far, move the apparatus closer to a hydrant.
~b~Hydrant connected.~s~ The ~y~{0}~s~ is now being supplied with water.
Power ~g~isolated~s~. Water is safe to use now.
The door is ~r~locked~s~. Force it with a ~y~halligan bar~s~ or ~y~axe~s~ from the engine.
Carrying the ~b~PPV fan~s~. Press ~b~{0}~s~ in the doorway, facing in, to set it up.
~b~PPV fan~s~ running: the smoke is being pushed out. Mind the fire, it gets more air too.
~b~PPV fan~s~ running, but it isn't blowing into a burning building.
~b~{0}:~s~ Nothing left to do here, coming to you.
~b~{0}:~s~ Patient is out of the vehicle.
~o~None of your apparatus has a deck gun.
The door is ~r~jammed~s~. Get the ~y~hydraulic tools~s~ from an apparatus.
~o~Stabilize the vehicle with cribbing~s~ before using hydraulic tools.
Vehicle ~g~stabilized~s~. It is safe to use the hydraulic tools.
~b~Face piece on.~s~ Breathing from your cylinder ({0:P0}).
~r~PASS alarm~s~: you haven't moved for 30 seconds. Move to reset it.
~r~Your SCBA cylinder is empty!~s~ Get out of the smoke and swap it at an engine.
~o~Low air~s~: {0:P0} left. Head out and swap your cylinder at an engine.
~r~Your cylinder is empty!~s~ Get out of the smoke.
~r~You are breathing smoke!~s~ Put your face piece on with ~b~{0}~s~.
~r~Electric shock!~s~ Isolate the power first, or use an extinguisher.
~r~Too hot!~s~ Back off, or protect yourself with a ~b~fog~s~ pattern.
Thermal imaging camera taken. Press ~b~{0}~s~ to turn it on.
Vehicle model ~y~{0}~s~ does not exist, check Apparatus.xml.
Your ~y~{0}~s~ is ready in front of the station.
~y~{0}~s~ from {1} is en route to the scene.
The supply line of your ~y~{0}~s~ snapped off the hydrant.
A patient is ready for transport, an ambulance is on its way.
Stretcher model ~y~{0}~s~ doesn't exist, check LSFD.ini.
~b~{0}:~s~ Patient is on the stretcher, moving to the ambulance.
The patient was handed over at {0}.
A patient went into ~r~cardiac arrest~s~! Start CPR.
A patient is ~o~deteriorating~s~ and lost consciousness.
put the patient down (~o~still in danger~s~)
The patient is ~g~stable~s~. The ~b~ambulance~s~ crew will take them to hospital.
~g~Pulse is back!~s~ The patient was resuscitated.
Victim ~g~rescued~s~ from the building. Treat them for smoke inhalation.
Two vehicles, one occupant ~r~trapped~s~. Extrication required.
The car came right across the center line, hit them head on!
The driver isn't moving. I tried {0} door, it's jammed shut.
Stabilize the vehicle with ~y~cribbing~s~, force or cut a door with the ~y~hydraulic tools~s~, extricate and treat the ~r~patient~s~.
Rear-end collision, one driver complaining of neck pain.
They stopped all of a sudden and I couldn't brake in time. I'm so sorry.
I'm fine, but the other driver says the neck hurts.
Check the vehicles and treat the ~r~injured driver~s~.
Single vehicle rolled over, driver ~r~trapped~s~ upside down.
It clipped the curb and just flipped, it rolled over twice!
The driver's still hanging upside down in there. {0} was talking a minute ago.
The vehicle is on its roof: stabilize it with ~y~cribbing~s~ before cutting the ~r~driver~s~ out.
Motorcyclist down after a collision with a car.
I pulled out, I just didn't see {0} coming!
{0}'s not getting up. I didn't want to move {1}, {2} still has the helmet on.
Pedestrian hit by a vehicle, driver stayed on scene.
I didn't see {0}! {1} stepped out between the parked cars!
I was only doing thirty. {0} hit the windshield and landed over there.
Treat the ~r~pedestrian~s~. Start CPR if there is no pulse.
Pile-up with multiple patients and entrapment. ~o~Mass casualty incident~s~.

~o~Mass casualty incident~s~: ~y~triage~s~ every patient first (hold E), then treat ~r~red~s~, ~y~yellow~s~ and ~g~green~s~ in that order. Black means expectant: CPR only once the others are cared for.
Cordon ~g~in place~s~. Onlookers are moving back.
Construction crew hit a gas main, ~o~strong smell of gas~s~. Approach from upwind, no ignition sources.
We were digging for a water line and the excavator went right through the gas main.
The shut-off valve is under a cover in the street, a few meters from the hole. You need a bar to turn it.
The valve needs a ~y~halligan bar~s~ from the engine as a key.
Set up a ~y~cordon~s~ with traffic cones, then close the ~y~gas valve~s~. Any spark can ignite the gas.
Valve ~g~closed~s~. Let the gas clear and check the area with the gas detector.
Gas detector: ~g~0% LEL~s~. The gas company takes over.
The leak caught fire. Close the valve and protect the surroundings; don't put it out before the gas is off.
Vehicle with a ruptured fuel tank, ~o~fuel all over the roadway~s~. No injuries reported.
I hit something on the road and the tank split open. It's gasoline, it's everywhere.
Nobody's hurt. I turned the engine off and got out.
All fuel ~g~absorbed~s~. The road can be swept.
Cordon off the road with ~y~traffic cones~s~ and soak up the fuel with ~y~absorbent~s~ before it ignites.
The spill caught fire. Use ~y~foam~s~ on the burning fuel.
Everything is taken care of. Good work.
~y~{0}~s~. The fire alarm system went off, no caller on the line. Investigate.
Go inside and check the ~y~fire alarm panel~s~ to find out which detector went off.
Panel: ~y~detector fault~s~ in zone 3. No smoke, no fire.
Panel: smoke detector in the ~y~kitchen~s~. Somebody burnt their lunch.
Smoke and flames inside ~y~{0}~s~. Upgraded to a structure fire.
Alarm ~g~reset~s~. Building handed back to the owner.
~y~{0}~s~. Staff smell something burning, no visible smoke. Locate the source.
search for the ~y~source~s~ of the smell
Search the building. The ~y~thermal imaging camera~s~ shows heat behind walls.
~r~Overheated wiring~s~ is smoldering behind the wall!
Isolate the power at the panel (~y~yellow arrow~s~) before you use water.
Nothing found inside. Probably a barbecue next door.
~y~{0}~s~. CO detector sounding, occupants are outside.
Carbon monoxide is invisible: put your ~b~SCBA~s~ on ({0}) and measure with the ~y~gas detector~s~.
Gas detector: ~r~CO {0} ppm~s~. Get everyone out and ventilate!
Windows and doors open, the gas is clearing.
Gas detector: ~g~CO 0 ppm~s~. Tell the occupants to have the boiler checked.
Occupants are reported out of the building.
Talk to the ~y~caller~s~, search the building and ~r~carry the victims out~s~, then extinguish the ~r~fire~s~. Your crew can help from the tablet.
Stretch a ~b~hose line~s~ into the building and extinguish the ~r~fire~s~. The ~y~caller~s~ is waiting out front.
Put your ~b~SCBA~s~ face piece on ({0}) before you go into the smoke.
We all got out, thank God. Nobody's inside.
Please, help! My {0} is still inside, {1}!
{0} was screaming for help, now I can't hear {1} anymore!
There's more people in there, I don't know where!
It smelled like gas right before it went up.
It started in the kitchen, it spread so fast.
I heard a bang and then there was smoke everywhere.
The smoke alarm woke me up, the hallway was already full of smoke.
Where the caller last saw {0} is marked on your map.
Extinguish all the ~r~fires~s~ in the area ({0}).
Vegetation fire spreading along the road. Protect nearby structures.
Dumpster and trash fire behind a building, no exposures reported.
Fire at an industrial site, ~o~possible hazardous materials~s~. Approach from upwind.
Everyone on shift is out and accounted for.
There are drums of solvent stored behind that building. Keep your people away from the smoke!
~y~{0}~s~. Fire in the electrical room, ~o~power still on~s~.
~o~Live electrics~s~: water will shock you. ~y~Isolate the power~s~ at the panel first, or use an extinguisher.
An electric car is on fire, the battery is popping. ~o~Expect a long cooling job~s~.
It's electric! The battery started hissing and popping under the floor, and then it just went up.
I got out right away. Every time you think it's out, it flares up again.
~o~Lithium battery fire~s~: foam doesn't help, it takes a lot of water and it keeps rekindling. Keep cooling until the thermal camera shows no hotspots.
Vehicle fully involved, the driver got out with ~r~burn injuries~s~.
A vehicle is on fire on the roadway, the driver reportedly got out.
I smelled something burning, so I pulled over. Then the smoke came out from under the hood.
Everything I own is in that car.
Is it going to explode? There's a full tank in there.
The patient has ~r~no pulse~s~: start ~r~CPR~s~ right away and use an ~y~AED~s~ if you have one.
{0} just grabbed {1} chest and went down! {2}'s not breathing!
I tried to wake {0} up, nothing.
The dispatcher told me to push on {0} chest, I did, I don't know if I did it right.
Please, is {0} going to be okay?
{0} said {1} felt dizzy, and then {2} just collapsed.
{0} hit {1} head on the way down.
{0} tripped off the curb and fell hard.
{0} fell off a ladder, it was about three meters.
Some guy on a bike knocked {0} over and just rode off.
{0} was bleeding a lot, I gave {1} my jacket.
The patient could not be saved. Clear the call when you are ready.
Person collapsed, ~r~not breathing~s~. Bystander is on the phone.
Person found unresponsive on the sidewalk, breathing status unknown.
Person fell from a ladder, possible leg fracture.
Assault victim with lacerations, police are on scene.
Elderly person fell down the stairs.
Pan fire spreading to the cabinets, the occupant tried to put it out.
Put out the ~r~fire~s~ and treat the ~r~occupant~s~.
Fire out and the occupant is being cared for.
I heard the smoke alarm and saw flames in the kitchen window.
They tried to put it out with water. I think they burned their arms.
Caller smells gas in their garage, a resident feels dizzy.
Wear your ~b~SCBA~s~, take the ~y~gas detector~s~, find the leak and ventilate.
Gas ~g~off~s~, the garage is airing out.
Car hit a pole, driver ~r~trapped~s~, the passenger got out.
Stabilize the car, extricate the ~r~driver~s~ and check the ~y~passenger~s~.
